title: Status page component glossary + customer troubleshooting (Streaming, Embeddings, Rerank)
author: Elliot Price
release_notes: Docs: Added customer-facing glossary for status components (Streaming, Embeddings, Rerank) and troubleshooting steps aligned with our incident update templates.
description: Context: As part of the Status page transparency upgrades, we’re publishing a customer-friendly glossary for the new status components and a small set of troubleshooting steps that are consistent with (and referenced by) our incident communication templates. This is intended to reduce support back-and-forth during partial degradations (notably streaming-only failures) and to make it clearer what customers can do while we mitigate. What’s included: (1) New glossary page for status components with plain-language definitions, typical symptoms, and common causes (without internal service names/jargon). (2) New troubleshooting sections for Streaming, Embeddings, and Rerank with customer actions that match the template guidance (retry/backoff, region pinning, fallback model guidance where applicable). (3) Cross-links to the existing “How to read our status page” page and to relevant API docs where appropriate. Notes/constraints: We intentionally avoid promising specific SLAs or publishing sensitive implementation details; language was reviewed for disclosure boundaries (no provider attribution, no vulnerability-like detail). Content is written so it can be linked directly in status updates (short headings, scannable bullets). Example snippet (Streaming troubleshooting): If streaming responses disconnect early, confirm you are reading the response stream continuously, set an idle timeout >= 60s, and retry with exponential backoff; if your network path includes a proxy, ensure proxy buffering is disabled for event streams; if the issue is region-specific, consider temporarily pinning to an alternate region if your account is enabled. Checklist: - [x] Add glossary page + sidebar nav entry - [x] Add per-component troubleshooting sections (Streaming/Embeddings/Rerank) - [x] Keep language aligned to incident templates (Investigating/Identified/Monitoring/Resolved) - [x] Run link checker and fix anchors - [x] Confirm no internal jargon (e.g., “scheduler”) leaks into customer docs

conversation: Rafael Mendes (review): The glossary reads well. Two nits: (1) In Streaming section, avoid “scheduler/capacity queue” language—customers don’t need that. (2) Can we align the customer actions with our templates: mention “retry with exponential backoff” and “next update timing” phrasing only on the status page side, not in docs.

Elliot Price (author): Updated Streaming glossary to remove scheduler wording and replaced with “capacity constraints” phrasing. Also removed the “next update” reference from the docs sections; kept docs focused on actions + symptoms, and left cadence language to the status updates/templates.

Tomáš Novák (review): +1 overall. Request: add a short callout on how to interpret “Degraded performance” vs “Partial outage” for these components, and explicitly say that non-streaming requests may still succeed during a Streaming incident (to match SUP-18421 confusion).

Elliot Price (author): Added a “Impact states for this component” callout to each of Streaming/Embeddings/Rerank pages with examples (e.g., Streaming degraded while non-streaming responses succeed). Also added a one-liner to the glossary entry for Streaming: “Non-streaming requests may continue to succeed.”

Marissa Cole (review): Small copy request: In Rerank troubleshooting, please avoid implying we recommend switching providers/models. Keep it to “fallback to an alternate model/version if configured” and link to the model routing docs (internal link). Also, can we use the same component names as the status page (capitalization + exact strings)?

Elliot Price (author): Done. Adjusted the fallback language to “alternate model/version if your application is configured for it” and linked to our routing/fallback docs. Standardized capitalization and component strings across pages and sidebar.

Dev Patel (review): This will help Support macros a lot. Can we add a short “What info to include when contacting support” bullet list (request id, region, timestamp, model, error message)? That’s a frequent gap during incidents.
Elliot Price (author): Added a “If you need help” section on each component page with the info list. Kept it generic and consistent with our existing support contact guidance.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved. Thanks for keeping it customer-safe and aligned with the templates.
